slides.title: TeamCreator
slides.alt: TeamCreator: project delivery.

slides.title: Delivery coordination
slides.alt: Delivery coordination: the VP manages the portfolio while the PM manages people, deadlines and client commitments.

slides.title: PM discovery
slides.alt: PM discovery: 16 interviews overall. Six PMs spoken to at GigaHack, all six using Claude. Founder-reported discovery.

slides.title: Research
slides.alt: Research: analytics and visualization 53%, collaboration 53%, workflow automation 51%. Desired capabilities from Smartsheet PPM research.

slides.title: Digital twin
slides.alt: Digital twin: structured project state connects people, commitments, dependencies, history and decisions.

slides.title: PM workspace
slides.alt: PM workspace: the agent proposes tasks and decisions; the PM reviews evidence and retains final authority.

slides.title: VP portfolio
slides.alt: VP portfolio: an illustrative view of project progress, delivery risks and decisions across projects.

slides.title: MVP
slides.alt: MVP: a synthetic project demonstration linking context, people, tasks, scenarios and decisions.

slides.title: Risk scenarios
slides.alt: Risk scenarios: compare the baseline with an intervention under explicit model assumptions.

slides.title: Reporting
slides.alt: Reporting: draft progress and decision reports for clients and sponsors.

slides.title: Data and access
slides.alt: Data and access: a proposed privacy boundary for scoped project context and external AI access.

slides.title: Pricing
slides.alt: Pricing: proposed entry tier of 80 US dollars per project manager per month, with a free tier.

slides.title: Adoption
slides.alt: Adoption: PM discovery and early adopters can lead to champions inside organizations.

slides.title: Team
slides.alt: Team: Lucian, AI Stack Engineer, 4 years; Tudor, Serial Entrepreneur, 16 years; Cristian, ML and Backend Engineer, 5 years; Vadim, Innovation and Technology Transfer Expert, 14 years.

slides.title: Roadmap
slides.alt: Roadmap: product and pilot milestones for the next stage of TeamCreator.

slides.title: Differentiation
slides.alt: Differentiation. Jira/Rovo: work tracking and agent actions. Planner/Copilot: plans, portfolios and reports. RiskyProject: schedule and cost simulation. TeamCreator target: cross-tool context, scenarios and PM decisions. Integrations and added value remain to prove.
slides.question: How is this different from what already exists?

slides.title: Current state
slides.alt: Current state. Working: project views, scenario engine and report previews. Synthetic: people, tasks, demo sources and opening scenario. Planned: live connectors, installed AI host and shared VP portfolio. A local agent tool path was demonstrated separately.
slides.question: What's real, and what's mocked?

slides.title: Real data
slides.alt: Real data. Structured records lead to PM review and scenario comparison. Inputs include tasks, owners, dates and dependencies. Synthetic import verified; authorized customer-case evaluation is next.
slides.question: Does it work with real data?

slides.title: Pilot readiness
slides.alt: Pilot readiness. Approved project and data scope; secure environment and input path; PM review and scenario evaluation; agreed outcome measures. External AI requires its access and privacy boundary first.
slides.question: What would you need to go live with a first team?

slides.title: Production readiness
slides.alt: Production readiness. Access: identity and project permissions. Reliability: shared storage and recovery. Integrations: scoped sync and audit history. Operations: monitoring, support and privacy. The shared VP portfolio follows the same controls.
slides.question: What is still needed for an organization to rely on it?

slides.title: Simulation
slides.alt: Simulation. Inputs: duration ranges, dependencies, capacity and calendars. Monte Carlo produces completion ranges and compares baseline with intervention. Results are conditional on input assumptions; calibration remains to do.
slides.question: How do the predictions work, and how accurate are they?

slides.title: Data protection
slides.alt: Data protection. Target architecture: customer records, minimum scoped context, approved AI tool. Identity mapping stays customer-controlled. Context uses pseudonymous IDs and permitted history. Pseudonymization is not anonymization.
slides.question: What employee data goes to the AI?

slides.title: Agent actions
slides.alt: Agent actions. Agent: read context, run scenarios and propose changes. PM: review evidence, edit or reject, authorize changes. Target workflow; synthetic local tool path demonstrated; assistant integration planned.
slides.question: Can the AI make a decision or change a project by itself?

slides.title: Early adopters
slides.alt: Early adopters. A live milestone, cross-team dependency, accountable sponsor, approved data and repeat feedback. PM champion to delivery sponsor to organization. Initial segment to validate.
slides.question: Who will use this first, and how will you reach them?

slides.title: Pricing and value
slides.alt: Pricing and value. Proposed entry tier: 80 US dollars per PM per month. Five paid PMs cost 4,800 dollars a year. Value to validate: deadline exposure, action taken, outcome and contribution. No measured ROI is claimed.
slides.question: Who pays, why eighty dollars, and what is the return?

slides.title: Validation
slides.alt: Validation. Baseline: what did the PM already know? Decision: did the warning change an action? Outcome: what happened to the milestone? Record forecasts before outcomes; include errors and overrides.
slides.question: How will you prove this helps beyond a good-looking demo?

slides.title: Resources
slides.alt: Resources. A live project with a PM champion and delivery sponsor; an approved scoped case and data approver; repeated evaluation of decisions and milestone outcomes. Next gate: a supervised pilot.
slides.question: What do you need from us now?
